title: The tight-cut tree fixes creation between atoms joined through atoms
subject: Whether native creation between two lines is determined by their place in the tight-cut decomposition
conclusion: On 50 spaces, the native relation between two atom lines is a function of their place in the decomposition wherever the atoms are the same, adjacent or joined through atoms only (21 places, 10,074 pairs), with fixed rules for chains, siblings and co-receivers, while through plane glue it can depend on more. The source rule fixed from these rules counts the Heawood braces, and the genus, on all 47 spaces without a non-Fano brace.
